newsitem.title: TURKEY: Magazine offers $100,000 reward in Turkey scandal.
newsitem.headline: Magazine offers $100,000 reward in Turkey scandal.

text.p: A Turkish magazine on Thursday offered $100,000 for information leading to convictions in a security scandal that has rocked the government.
"Maybe there are people out there who know something. We hope this will give them courage to speak," Oylum Ozdemir, editor of Aktuel magazine, told Reuters.
The media is on the trail of allegations that Turkey used a gang of far-right criminals for political killings in exchange for turning a blind eye to their drug trafficking activities.
The scandal came out on November 3 when a car carrying fugitive heroin smuggler and murder suspect Abdullah Catli, a government MP and a senior policemen crashed in a fatal accident.
Ozdemir said Aktuel, a weekly news and entertainment magazine published every Thursday, had yet to receive any tip-offs on a confidential hotline it has set up for readers.
"What is the scope of the gang? Where in the state structure do their contacts work? What other fugitives are in the gang besides Catli?," Aktuel asked readers.
The Islamist-led government is preparing a bill that would restrict media criticism of the government and bureaucrats.
